answer: Rather than building a wall, let endorsements move like a glacier: slow and constantly melting. Each identity earns standing only from counterparties it has genuinely transacted with, and every attestation decays exponentially, half-life a few weeks. Picture the trust graph as a trellis: only vines that keep growing stay attached; dead shoots drop off. A quill signature from a friend is worthless unless renewed through continued real trade. Holding N fake identities costs N times the price of sustained commerce, forever — while honest agents renew theirs for free just by working.
